data.short_meaning: Shining light, torch of the sun
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Helene is derived from Helios, the Greek god of the sun. The name Helene means 'shining light' or 'torch of the sun'. In Greek mythology, Helene was the daughter of King Priam of Troy and the sister of Hector. She was famed for her beauty, which led to the Trojan War. The name Helene carries the meaning “Shining light, torch of the sun” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Helene usually hope their child will grow to embody shining light, torch of the sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Helene total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_latin.name: Helene

In Christian tradition, Saint Helena, the mother of Emperor Constantine, is revered for her piety and her role in the discovery of the True Cross. The name Helene has been associated with these virtues, symbolizing a person who brings light, peace, and happiness to others.

data.cultural_impact: The Christian name Helene was popular during the Middle Ages in Europe, especially in France. It is believed that the name became associated with the Christian saints Helena of Constantinople and Helena of Avaricum. Helena of Constantinople is most famous for her discovery of the True Cross and other relics of Christ, while Helena of Avaricum was a bishop and also a noted scholar and poet. The name Helene continued to be in use throughout the Renaissance and beyond, becoming particularly popular in the French-speaking world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Helene holds spiritual significance for Christians as a reminder of the light of God in our lives. Just as the sun represents light and illumination in Greek mythology, the name Helene symbolizes the light of Christ that shines within us and guides us on our spiritual journey. In addition, the name is linked to the saints Helena of Constantinople and Helena of Avaricum, who are models of faith, perseverance, and spiritual insight. Their stories remind us of the power of faith to reveal truth and transform lives.
